page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is an x86_64 architecture cloud server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 3 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 320 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate a profile suited for moderate workloads. Single-core processing is weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1272.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 796.0. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core reaching 6774.42. Memory read bandwidth is average at 407.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 48.31 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 18.72 GB/sec. Text processing and compression tasks show poor performance, with gzip compression single-threaded scoring 18.3 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression multi-threaded scoring 19.84 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, making the instance susceptible to resource contention under sustained heavy loads. Qualitatively, this server offers high resource density and storage capacity for budget-conscious deployments, balancing 6 vCPUs and 320 GB of fast NVMe storage. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads that do not require sustained peak CPU performance, such as light web serving, development environments, basic database operations, and small-scale text or image processing tasks.
